_about: Plain-language text for GRAP stages, AQI categories, pollutants and every Cedar policy (by @id). It explains; it never changes a decision.

1.name: Poor air
1.about: First steps across Delhi-NCR: dust control at building sites, no open burning, strict pollution checks on vehicles, diesel generators and older buses kept in check.
measures: Building and demolition sites must keep dust down: cover materials, sprinkle water, run anti-smog guns and wash vehicle wheels. Large sites are registered and monitored.
No open burning of garbage, leaves or other waste.
Roads are swept by machine and sprinkled with water to settle dust.
Strict checks on vehicle pollution certificates (PUC) and on vehicles giving out visible smoke.
Diesel generators may run only if they meet emission standards or have approved pollution controls; hospitals, lifts and other emergency services are exempt.
BS-IV and older buses from other NCR and neighbouring states are kept out of Delhi; electric, CNG and BS-VI buses can come in.

2.name: Very poor air
2.about: Stage I plus more: daily road cleaning with dust suppressants, higher parking fees, more buses and metro trips, and people asked to use public transport.
measures: Daily machine sweeping and water sprinkling with dust suppressants on main roads and pollution hotspots.
Parking fees go up to discourage private vehicles.
More CNG and electric buses and more metro trips.
Public office timings in Delhi are staggered to spread out the rush.
Citizens are asked to use public transport and keep personal vehicle use to a minimum.

3.name: Severe air
3.about: Stage I and II plus: dusty construction stopped, older petrol and diesel cars off the road, hybrid classes up to Class V.
measures: Dust-generating construction and demolition stops: digging, piling, demolition, brick and masonry work, painting, tile cutting and road building. Railway, metro, airport, hospital, defence, sanitation and linear public projects are exempt.
BS-III petrol and BS-IV (or older) diesel cars are barred in Delhi and nearby NCR districts, now including Sonipat. Cars adapted for people with disabilities are exempt.
Diesel BS-IV (or older) light and medium goods vehicles registered outside Delhi cannot enter, with no exemption for essential goods.
Classes up to Class V in Delhi move to hybrid mode; families can choose online classes.
The Delhi and NCR governments can decide to let half of office staff work from home.

4.name: Severe+ air
4.about: Emergency level: most trucks barred, all big construction stopped, hybrid classes for more grades, and the advice to stay indoors as much as possible.
measures: BS-IV and older diesel trucks cannot enter Delhi; essential-goods trucks are no longer exempt.
Linear public projects such as highways, roads, flyovers and power lines also stop.
Classes VI to IX and XI in Delhi move to hybrid mode.
State governments can add emergency steps such as odd-even for cars or closing non-emergency businesses.
Children, older people and anyone with lung or heart disease are advised to stay indoors as much as possible and wear a mask outside.

category_impact.Satisfactory: Minor breathing discomfort for sensitive people.
category_impact.Moderate: Breathing discomfort for people with lung disease such as asthma, and for people with heart disease, children and older adults.
category_impact.Poor: Breathing discomfort for most people on long exposure.
category_impact.Severe: Affects healthy people and seriously affects people who are already ill.

pollutants.PM2.5: PM2.5: fine particles from traffic, smoke and burning. Small enough to reach deep into the lungs and the blood.
pollutants.PM10: PM10: coarser dust from roads, building work and soil. It irritates the nose, throat and airways.

athlete.training.below_stage4.means: You can train outdoors. GRAP does not limit exercise at this stage.
athlete.training.below_stage4.why: GRAP only asks people to cut outdoor activity at Stage IV, the worst level.
athlete.training.below_stage4.do: Still train at the cleanest hour shown here: hard exercise makes you breathe in many times more air.

athlete.training.stage4_charter.means: At Stage IV, GRAP asks everyone to cut outdoor activity that is not essential, and a training run counts.
athlete.training.stage4_charter.why: The air is severe. Hard exercise makes you breathe five to ten times more air, so you take in far more pollution.
athlete.training.stage4_charter.do: Train indoors (gym, treadmill, home workout) or take a rest day. This is advice, not a ban.

commuter.bs3_petrol_bs4_diesel_car.stage.means: You cannot drive a BS-III petrol or BS-IV (or older) diesel car in Delhi while Stage III or IV is in force.
commuter.bs3_petrol_bs4_diesel_car.stage.why: Older engines give out far more smoke and fine particles. Taking them off the road is one of the quickest ways to cut pollution.
commuter.bs3_petrol_bs4_diesel_car.stage.do: Take the metro or a bus, share a ride, or use a newer BS-VI car. Cars adapted for people with disabilities are exempt. Your car's BS level is on its registration certificate (RC).

commuter.bs3_petrol_bs4_diesel_car.below.means: You can drive this car today. The ban on older petrol and diesel cars only starts at Stage III.
commuter.bs3_petrol_bs4_diesel_car.below.why: GRAP adds rules step by step as the air gets worse.
commuter.bs3_petrol_bs4_diesel_car.below.do: Keep a valid PUC certificate: checks get stricter on bad-air days.

commuter.private_car.stage2_charter.means: From Stage II, GRAP asks people to leave the car at home and use public transport. It is advice, not a ban: a BS-VI car may still be driven.
commuter.private_car.stage2_charter.why: Traffic is one of Delhi's biggest sources of PM2.5 in winter. Fewer cars means cleaner air for everyone, you included.
commuter.private_car.stage2_charter.do: Take the metro or a bus, or share a ride for today.

commuter.private_car.below_stage2.why: GRAP only asks people to cut car use from Stage II.
commuter.private_car.below_stage2.do: In heavy traffic, keep the windows up and the air on recirculate.

commuter.office.below_stage3.means: Go to the office as usual. GRAP does not change office attendance at this stage.
commuter.office.below_stage3.why: Work-from-home steps only come in at Stage III and above, and the state government decides them.

commuter.lunch_walk.below_stage4.means: A short walk is fine as far as GRAP goes.
commuter.lunch_walk.below_stage4.why: GRAP only advises against non-essential outdoor activity at Stage IV.
commuter.lunch_walk.below_stage4.do: Walk at the cleanest hour, on quieter streets away from traffic.

commuter.lunch_walk.stage4_charter.means: At Stage IV, GRAP asks everyone to cut outdoor activity that is not essential. A lunch walk is one to skip.
commuter.lunch_walk.stage4_charter.why: Air this bad harms even healthy people.
commuter.lunch_walk.stage4_charter.do: Walk indoors instead: corridors, stairs or a mall. Eat lunch inside.

older.outdoor.stage4_charter.means: At Stage IV, GRAP advises older people and people with lung, heart or long-term illness to stay indoors as much as possible.
older.outdoor.stage4_charter.why: Severe air can bring on breathing trouble, heart attacks and strokes, and the risk is highest for these groups.
older.outdoor.stage4_charter.do: Walk at home or indoors. If you must go out, keep it short, wear a well-fitted N95 and go at the cleanest hour.

older.outdoor.below_stage4.means: GRAP does not limit walks or errands at this stage.
older.outdoor.below_stage4.why: The advice to stay indoors starts at Stage IV.
older.outdoor.below_stage4.do: Still go at the cleanest hour, and keep it gentle on poor-air days.

rider.two_wheeler.below_stage4.means: You can ride your shift. GRAP does not limit two-wheelers at this stage.
rider.two_wheeler.below_stage4.why: No rule for two-wheelers is part of Stages I to III.
rider.two_wheeler.below_stage4.do: A well-fitted N95 under the helmet helps a lot. Take your break off the road at the worst hour.

rider.outside_lgv.stage3.means: A BS-IV or older diesel light goods vehicle (a small truck or tempo) registered outside Delhi cannot enter Delhi at Stage III or IV.
rider.outside_lgv.stage3.why: Older diesel goods vehicles give out a lot of soot.
rider.outside_lgv.stage3.do: Use a Delhi-registered BS-VI, CNG or electric vehicle, and check the order for exemptions for essential goods.

rider.outside_lgv.below_stage3.means: This vehicle can run today. The entry ban starts at Stage III.
rider.outside_lgv.below_stage3.why: GRAP adds rules step by step as the air gets worse.

rider.mgv.stage3.means: BS-IV or older diesel medium goods vehicles cannot run in Delhi at Stage III or IV, and those registered outside Delhi cannot enter.
rider.mgv.stage3.why: Older diesel goods vehicles give out a lot of soot.
rider.mgv.stage3.do: Switch to a BS-VI, CNG or electric vehicle, and check the order for exemptions for essential goods.

rider.mgv.below_stage3.means: This vehicle can run today. The ban starts at Stage III.
rider.mgv.below_stage3.why: GRAP adds rules step by step as the air gets worse.

school.primary_hybrid.stage3.means: Classes up to Class V must also run online. Families can choose to study from home.
school.primary_hybrid.stage3.why: Young children breathe faster and are harmed more by polluted air, and the trip to school adds to it.
school.primary_hybrid.stage3.do: Choose online classes if the school offers them, and check the school's notice for today.

school.primary_in_person.below_stage3.means: Classes up to Class V run in person as usual.
school.primary_in_person.below_stage3.why: Online classes for these grades only start at Stage III.

school.senior_hybrid.stage4.means: Classes VI to IX and XI must also run online at Stage IV. Families can choose to study from home.
school.senior_hybrid.stage4.why: At the worst level of pollution, GRAP cuts how many children travel to school.
school.senior_hybrid.stage4.do: Choose online if offered. Classes X and XII are not covered by this rule.

school.senior_in_person.below_stage4.means: Classes VI to IX and XI run in person as usual.
school.senior_in_person.below_stage4.why: Online classes for these grades only start at Stage IV.

school.outdoor_activity.stage4_charter.means: At Stage IV, GRAP advises that children stay indoors as much as possible, so assembly, recess and sport should move inside.
school.outdoor_activity.stage4_charter.why: Children breathe more air for their size, and their lungs are still growing.
school.outdoor_activity.stage4_charter.do: Hold assembly in the hall or classrooms, and do indoor games or stretches instead of outdoor PE.

school.outdoor_activity.below_stage4.means: GRAP does not stop outdoor school activities at this stage.
school.outdoor_activity.below_stage4.why: The Delhi Education Department sometimes issues its own circular, so watch for one.
school.outdoor_activity.below_stage4.do: Use the cleanest hour of the school day for sport.

charter.sensitive_groups.stage4.means: Because of your age or health, GRAP's Stage IV advice is to stay indoors as much as possible, and this is outdoors.
charter.sensitive_groups.stage4.why: Children, pregnant women, older people and people with lung, heart, stroke or long-term illness are hurt most by severe air.
charter.sensitive_groups.stage4.do: Keep it indoors or skip it today. If you must go out, wear a well-fitted N95 and keep it short.

worker.dusty_cnd.stage3.means: Dusty construction work (digging, demolition, brickwork, tile cutting, road work) has to stop across NCR at Stage III and IV.
worker.dusty_cnd.stage3.why: Building dust is one of the biggest sources of PM10 in Delhi.
worker.dusty_cnd.stage3.do: Switch to less dusty work such as finishing, plumbing or electrical if your site allows. Railway, metro, airport, hospital, defence and sanitation projects are exempt. Registered construction workers have received support payments during past bans: ask your union or the construction workers' welfare board.

worker.dusty_cnd.below_stage3.means: The work can go on, but the site must control dust: water spraying, covered sand and soil, screens around the site.
worker.dusty_cnd.below_stage3.why: Stages I and II cut dust without stopping work.
worker.dusty_cnd.below_stage3.do: Wear a well-fitted N95 for the dustiest jobs.

worker.other_cnd.permitted.means: Less dusty work like finishing, plumbing, carpentry and electrical can carry on.
worker.other_cnd.permitted.why: GRAP only stops the dustiest work; the rest must follow dust-control rules.
worker.other_cnd.permitted.do: Wear an N95 when there is dust in the air.

worker.outdoor_shift.below_stage4.means: GRAP does not stop outdoor work in general at this stage.
worker.outdoor_shift.below_stage4.why: Only specific dusty or polluting work is restricted below Stage IV.
worker.outdoor_shift.below_stage4.do: Take your break indoors at the worst hour, and drink plenty of water.

travel.public_transport.means: Travel by metro or bus as usual. GRAP never stops them; from Stage II it adds more buses and metro trips.
travel.public_transport.why: Public transport is how GRAP wants people to travel on bad-air days: fewer cars means less smoke and dust.
travel.public_transport.do: Keep the walk to the station short, and wait away from the kerb.

travel.on_foot_or_cycle.below_stage4.means: You can walk or cycle as usual. GRAP does not limit it before Stage IV.
travel.on_foot_or_cycle.below_stage4.why: GRAP's rules are about the sources of pollution, not about people moving on foot or by bike.
travel.on_foot_or_cycle.below_stage4.do: Pick quieter streets away from heavy traffic, and wear an N95 on busy roads if the air is Poor or worse.

travel.two_wheeler.below_stage4.means: You can ride your scooter or motorbike as usual. No Stage I to III action restricts two-wheelers.
travel.two_wheeler.below_stage4.why: The vehicle bans that come in at Stage III are for older cars and goods vehicles.
travel.two_wheeler.below_stage4.do: Keep its PUC certificate valid, and wear a well-fitted N95 under the helmet.

travel.auto.below_stage4.means: Autos and cabs run as usual. Delhi's autos run on CNG, which GRAP does not restrict before Stage IV.
travel.auto.below_stage4.why: GRAP targets older petrol and diesel vehicles; CNG and electric ones stay on the road.
travel.auto.below_stage4.do: Autos are open to traffic fumes, so an N95 helps on long rides.

outdoor_shift.means: At Stage IV, the government may add steps such as odd-even or closing some businesses. Whether they touch your work depends on the day's order.
outdoor_shift.why: Stage IV is the emergency level, and these steps are announced by the Delhi government.
outdoor_shift.do: Check the Delhi government order and your app's notices before your shift.

outdoor_work_shift.means: At Stage IV, the government may close non-emergency work. Whether your site is covered depends on the day's order.
outdoor_work_shift.why: Stage IV is the emergency level, and these steps are announced by the Delhi government.
outdoor_work_shift.do: Ask your contractor or site office, and check the Delhi government order.

office_attendance.means: At Stage III and IV, the Delhi government can ask offices to let half their staff work from home. It is not automatic.
office_attendance.why: Fewer people travelling means less traffic pollution.
office_attendance.do: Check your employer's notice and the Delhi government order for today. Work from home if you can.

school_commute.means: GRAP has no rule about the trip to school itself.
school_commute.why: The rules cover vehicles and schools, not people travelling.
school_commute.do: Prefer the school bus or metro over a private car, and keep the walk away from main roads.

morning_commute.means: GRAP has no rule about the trip itself.
morning_commute.why: The rules cover vehicles, not people travelling. See the car rules here if you drive.
morning_commute.do: The metro or a bus is the cleaner choice on a bad-air day.

evening_commute.means: GRAP has no rule about the trip itself.
evening_commute.why: The rules cover vehicles, not people travelling. See the car rules here if you drive.
evening_commute.do: The metro or a bus is the cleaner choice on a bad-air day.

travel_car.means: Whether you can drive depends on your car's fuel and BS level, which we don't know yet.
travel_car.why: From Stage III, GRAP takes BS-III petrol and BS-IV (or older) diesel cars off Delhi's roads.
travel_car.do: Add your car in your profile to see its exact rule. Your car's BS level is on its registration certificate (RC).

travel_walk.means: At Stage IV the governments can add emergency steps, such as odd-even or closing some businesses, so check today's order.
travel_walk.why: Stage IV is the emergency level; its extra steps are announced by the Delhi and NCR governments.
travel_walk.do: Check the Delhi government's order for today before you set out.

travel_cycle.means: At Stage IV the governments can add emergency steps, such as odd-even or closing some businesses, so check today's order.
travel_cycle.why: Stage IV is the emergency level; its extra steps are announced by the Delhi and NCR governments.
travel_cycle.do: Check the Delhi government's order for today before you set out.

travel_two_wheeler.means: At Stage IV the governments can add emergency steps, such as odd-even or closing some businesses, so check today's order.
travel_two_wheeler.why: Stage IV is the emergency level; its extra steps are announced by the Delhi and NCR governments.
travel_two_wheeler.do: Check the Delhi government's order for today before you set out.

travel_auto.means: At Stage IV the governments can add emergency steps, such as odd-even or closing some businesses, so check today's order.
travel_auto.why: Stage IV is the emergency level; its extra steps are announced by the Delhi and NCR governments.
travel_auto.do: Check the Delhi government's order for today before you set out.

uncovered_default.means: GRAP's schedule does not cover this, so we cannot say it is allowed.
uncovered_default.why: We only say Allowed when a rule says so.
uncovered_default.do: Check the latest CAQM order, or ask your employer or school.

verdict_meaning.go: The air stays within your safe range for normal outdoor activity.
verdict_meaning.limit: Go out if you need to, but keep it short and easy, and mask up.
verdict_meaning.stay_in: The air is above your limit for outdoor activity: keep it indoors where you can.

unknown.title: Stage unknown
unknown.sub: Not enough forecast data to estimate it.

headlines.none_okay: Delhi's air is {category}. GRAP starts at AQI {stage1_min}.
headlines.none_moderate: Delhi's average is {gap} points below Stage I, which starts at AQI {stage1_min}.

draft_rule.means: The rule we have for this is a draft that has not been checked against the latest CAQM order.
draft_rule.why: We only give an answer when the rule is verified.

estimate.label: Our estimate from Delhi's average AQI

grap._about: Text for the GRAP section. Sources: CAQM's GRAP schedule Rev. 29.09.2026 and PIB's release on it.
grap.intro: GRAP, the Graded Response Action Plan, is Delhi-NCR's step-by-step plan for bad air. CAQM, the air quality commission, switches it on for the whole of Delhi-NCR at once, not one neighbourhood at a time. As Delhi's AQI climbs, each stage adds rules on top of the ones before.
grap.city_line: Delhi's average AQI is {aqi} ({category}): the 24-hour AQI of {count} areas, averaged.
grap.city_line_forecast: Delhi's average AQI is forecast at {aqi} ({category}), across {count} areas.
grap.area_line: {area}: AQI {aqi}, the same figure as the air dials. GRAP still follows Delhi's average.
grap.area_basis: Not enough areas had a forecast, so this uses {area}'s AQI alone.
grap.next_line: Stage {label} starts at AQI {min_aqi}: {gap} points to go.
grap.next_reached: Delhi's AQI is already in the Stage {label} range (from {min_aqi}).
grap.top_line: Stage IV is the highest stage.
grap.outlook_worse: Tomorrow's forecast for Delhi points to Stage {label} (AQI {aqi}). CAQM can switch a stage on early when the forecast says the air is getting worse.
grap.outlook_better: Tomorrow's forecast for Delhi is better: {label_text} (AQI {aqi}).
grap.differs: Our estimate from Delhi's AQI is {estimate}.
grap.actions_count: {count} actions in the schedule. The main ones:
how: CAQM's GRAP sub-committee watches Delhi's average AQI from CPCB's monitoring stations, and the IMD and IITM forecasts.
When the AQI reaches a stage's range, or is forecast to, it orders that stage for all of Delhi-NCR. It can act a few days early.
Stages add up: Stage III means the Stage I, II and III actions all apply.
When the air improves for a while, CAQM revokes the stage. A revoked stage's rules stop applying.
Delhi and the NCR states can also issue their own extra orders on top of GRAP.
estimate: When the Saans Compass team has entered CAQM's latest order, the stage shown is that order.
Otherwise it is our estimate from Delhi's AQI, worked out like CPCB's: each area's 24-hour average, then the average across Delhi.
Our numbers come from the Open-Meteo forecast model, not CPCB's stations, so they can be some points off. Near a stage's edge, the official stage may differ.
grap.box_area: {area}: AQI {aqi} ({category}) over the last 24 hours, as in the air dials.
grap.box_area_tomorrow: {area} tomorrow: AQI {aqi} ({category}), the forecast day average.
grap.box_city: Delhi's average: AQI {aqi} ({category}). GRAP is set on this one figure for all of Delhi-NCR.
grap.fitted_none: Add your work, travel, car and health in your profile to fit these rules to you.
grap.charter_you: Because of {reasons}, GRAP's Stage IV advice to stay indoors as much as possible is meant for you.
